$meta.readThisFirst: Singh's own instructions already carry most of the functional spec, verbatim: "user can select the columns he want to see in table" + "rearrange the table columns by simply drag and drop the columns from 6 dots." That is followed literally below. What Figma does NOT specify and this contract had to leave open: what the two group headings represent (real category names were never entered — every one reads the placeholder "GROUP HEADING"), what the single ungrouped row above them means, where a newly-checked column lands in the visible order, and whether the panel scrolls past a fixed height. All four are recorded under notVerified, not guessed.

anatomy.panelContainerNote: A flex column, 400px wide in the measured frame, background surface/base, drop-shadow only (no border) on all four sides. Four direct children stacked with an 8px gap: header, search, list, footer.

searchField.value: Needs a programmatic label (aria-label or a visually-hidden <label>) beyond the placeholder — placeholder text alone is not an accessible name.
searchField.note: Not specified in Figma; standard WCAG requirement, not a design choice.

rowSemantics.value: Each row is a checkbox with a visible label — <input type="checkbox"> + <label>, not a styled <div> — consistent with UIG-008 in this design system's own CSS rules.

dragReorderKeyboardAlternative.value: NO KEYBOARD-ACCESSIBLE ALTERNATIVE TO DRAG EXISTS IN THIS FIGMA MEASUREMENT. Drag-and-drop reordering by mouse/touch only, with no visible 'move up' / 'move down' control or documented keyboard interaction, fails WCAG 2.1 SC 2.1.1 (Keyboard) as designed. This is the single most important gap in this contract.

closeButtonTouchTarget.value: 24x24 hit area is below the system's own documented --touch-target-min convention (referenced elsewhere in this design system). See defect D7.

defects: D1 — TWO DIFFERENT FIGMA COMPONENTS SHARE THE IDENTICAL NAME 'ddm rows - checkboxes + drag feature': node 13095:43335 (the one Singh linked — older, references legacy checkbox nodes 77:16/72:599, always renders checked+draggable with no exposed toggle in this usage) and node 27307:43097 (newer, references current Checkbox atom 27194:66388, has the confusingly-named unChecked toggle — see D3). The pattern uses BOTH in the same list: 27307:43097 for the top ungrouped row and the six 'available' rows, 13095:43335 for the twelve 'visible' rows. Any tool building from 'the atom Singh linked' alone would build only half the pattern correctly. Needs Figma AI to either retire one as an alias of the other, or document why two exist.

D2 — CODE-VS-RENDER DISCREPANCY on the ungrouped top row. The generated reference code's conditional logic implies a drag handle should render on that row (unChecked=false, drag defaults true), but the actual rendered screenshot shows no drag handle on it — visually flush-left, aligned differently from the twelve draggable rows below. Recorded as observed rather than resolved; the screenshot was trusted over the generated code's branching, consistent with this session's standing practice, but this needs a live Figma confirmation, not an assumption.

D3 — THE 'unChecked' VARIANT PROPERTY IS NAMED BACKWARDS on node 13095:43335. 'unChecked=Yes' (the default) renders a CHECKED row; 'unChecked=No' renders an UNCHECKED row. Confirmed directly from the six variant names in the component set (State=Default/Active/Hover x unChecked=Yes/No) cross-read against the generated JSX's conditional branches. This is the same class of defect as inverted booleans found elsewhere in this system (e.g. the DDM checkbox/radio selected-state work) — flag to Figma AI, do not propagate the backwards name into any built implementation.

D4 — fonts/tracking/X-tracking-0 is bound throughout (header title, search placeholder, row labels, group heading, footer buttons) — the same legacy name found system-wide this session, now confirmed present in an 8th place. One Figma rename still closes all of them.

D5 — the Apply button binds colors/X-Brandblue-600 rather than action/primary/bg for the identical #0077ff value — another legacy-prefixed name, not previously seen in this exact form on another Agency component contract this session.

D6 — control/height-default (=30) is bound on the search field and implied on rows/footer buttons, but is absent from the owner's variable export — the same known gap recorded on Button, Fields, Empty States and the DDM backlog.

D7 — the header close button's 22px glyph sits inside a 24px hit area with 3px padding (18px of clear space) — a 2px-per-side overflow of the icon past its own padding. Small, but the same defect class (icon overflowing its padding box) already flagged once this session on a different component (empty-states icon, +6px overflow) — worth a single Figma-side fix pass across all icon-in-padded-box instances rather than one-off patches.

D8 — no group category was ever entered. Both group headings in the measured instance read the literal placeholder text 'GROUP HEADING' — real category names (e.g. 'Visible Columns' / 'Available Columns', or per-table category names) were never authored in Figma, so this contract cannot publish real copy — see notVerified.

openTokenDecision.proposal: 1) Resolve D1 — one canonical row atom, not two. 2) Fix D3's inverted boolean name. 3) Rename fonts/tracking/X-tracking-0 (D4) and colors/X-Brandblue-600 (D5) to their non-legacy equivalents — both renames already requested elsewhere in this backlog, this is now an 8th and a 1st sighting respectively. 4) Decide whether control/height-default (D6) should enter the export.
openTokenDecision.gate: Design-owner approval required before any of these become bindings.
openTokenDecision.untilApproved: Every affected value is published RAW with the defect recorded. Recording a value here is NOT permission to hardcode it.

notVerified: What the two group headings represent in real use. Singh's instructions describe checked+draggable vs unchecked+non-draggable clearly, but not what CATEGORY divides the groups — read here as 'currently shown' vs 'available', which is the standard convention for this exact UI pattern (Notion/Airtable/Linear-style column pickers), but that is an assumption, not something Figma or Singh specified. Confirm before shipping copy.

What the single ungrouped row above the groups means. Could be a 'select all' control, a pinned/always-visible column (e.g. a row-selection or actions column that can't be hidden), or something else. Not documented anywhere in Figma — no annotation exists on this row.

Where a newly-checked 'available' column lands once checked. Assumed: appended to the end of the visible list, then draggable like any other visible row — the standard convention, not a measured or stated behaviour.

Whether the panel has a maximum height with internal scrolling once the column list is long. The measured instance shows 12+6=18 rows fitting inside a 900px demo frame with no scroll affordance visible or documented. A real table could have far more columns than that. No max-height was measured — same class of gap already flagged on a DDM assembled-menu node (1728:1) earlier in this backlog.
Whether 400px is a fixed panel width or should respond to viewport size. No breakpoint variant exists in Figma.
Any state for a row when its column is currently sorted, pinned, or otherwise not a plain show/hide/reorder case (e.g. a required column that cannot be hidden). Not present in the measured instance.
